mn-204C.35.citation: Minn. Stat. 204C.35 (recounts: federal, state and judicial races)

mn-204C.36.citation: Minn. Stat. 204C.36 (recounts in county, school district and municipal elections)

mn-208-full.citation: Minn. Stat. chapter 208 (presidential electors), whole chapter, for 208.05 (State Canvassing Board)

mn-const.citation: Constitution of the State of Minnesota, Article IV, section 6 (each house judge of its members' elections)

ties.applies_to: "an office" in a state primary ("nomination") or a general election, in the chapter that governs elections generally
ties.steps: the canvassing board with the responsibility for declaring the results for that office determines the tie by lot
ties.who: the canvassing board for that office

sources.quote: In case of a tie vote for nomination or election to an office, the canvassing board with the responsibility for declaring the results for that office shall determine the tie by lot.

ties.note: The text says "an office" and does not name federal, state or local offices, so it is read as covering all of them [inferred]; a municipal charter may say otherwise and was not read. For the legislature, the Constitution (Art. IV, sec. 6) makes each house "the judge of the election returns and eligibility of its own members"; so a legislative seat can still be taken up by the house after the lot.

ties.applies_to: presidential electors and alternates, in the general election (Minn. Stat. 208.05, State Canvassing Board)
ties.steps: when more than the number of persons to be elected as presidential electors or alternates have the highest and an equal number of votes, the secretary of state, in the presence of the State Canvassing Board, decides by lot which are declared elected; no such drawing is conducted if the Agreement Among the States to Elect the President by National Popular Vote governs the appointment of electors
ties.who: the secretary of state, in the presence of the State Canvassing Board

sources.quote: When it appears that more than the number of persons to be elected as presidential electors or alternates have the highest and an equal number of votes, the secretary of state, in the presence of the board shall decide by lot which of the persons shall be declared elected

ties.note: Minn. Stat. 208.05. The exception for the National Popular Vote agreement is in the same sentence of the section.

ties.steps: no provision for a tie on a ballot question was found
ties.note: Read: Minn. Stat. 204C.34, 204C.35 and 204C.36 and a search of chapters 204D and 208 (whole) for the words of a tie. 204C.34 speaks of a tie vote "for nomination or election to an office" only.

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes counted for that office
threshold.conditions: the vote-count alternative (10 votes or less) applies only if 400 votes or fewer were cast for the office
threshold.in_words: a margin under one-half of one percent, or ten votes or less where 400 votes or fewer were cast

who_may_request: the candidate whose election is in question, in writing
recounts.cost_bearer: jurisdiction (the manual recount is at no cost to the candidate within the thresholds)

sources.quote: (b) In a state general election when the difference between the votes of a candidate who would otherwise be declared elected to: (1) a state legislative office is less than one-half of one percent of the total number of votes counted for that office or is ten votes or less and the total number of votes cast for the office is 400 votes or less

recounts.note: The board recounts manually on the candidate's written request; there is no recount without the request, so this is a requested recount that costs the candidate nothing, not an automatic one. Request due by 5:00 p.m. on the second day after the canvass (204C.35 subd. 1(b)).

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes counted for that office
threshold.conditions: the vote-count alternative applies only if 400 votes or fewer were cast for the office
threshold.in_words: a margin under one-quarter of one percent, or ten votes or less where 400 votes or fewer were cast

who_may_request: the candidate whose election is in question, in writing
recounts.cost_bearer: jurisdiction (no cost to the candidate within the thresholds)

sources.quote: a statewide federal office, state constitutional office, statewide judicial office, congressional office, or district judicial office and the votes of any other candidate for that office is less than one-quarter of one percent of the total number of votes counted for that office

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes counted for that nomination
threshold.conditions: the vote-count alternative (10 votes or less) applies only if 400 votes or fewer were cast for the nomination; the difference must determine the nomination
threshold.in_words: in a state primary for a state legislative office, a margin under one-half of one percent, or ten votes or less where 400 votes or fewer were cast

who_may_request: the candidate whose nomination is in question, in writing, received by the filing officer by 5:00 p.m. on the second day after the canvass of the primary
recounts.cost_bearer: no cost to the candidate (the candidate is notified of the option to request a recount at no cost)

sources.quote: In a state primary when the difference between the votes cast for the candidates for nomination to: (1) a state legislative office is less than one-half of one percent of the total number of votes counted for that nomination or is ten votes or less and the total number of votes cast for the nomination is 400 votes or less

recounts.note: Minn. Stat. 204C.35 subd. 1(a)(1). The paragraph's closing words: the canvassing board "shall manually recount the vote upon receiving a written request from the candidate whose nomination is in question".

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes counted for that nomination
threshold.conditions: the vote-count alternative applies only if 400 votes or fewer were cast for the nomination; the difference must determine the nomination
threshold.in_words: in a state primary for a statewide federal, state constitutional, statewide judicial, congressional or district judicial office, a margin under one-quarter of one percent, or ten votes or less where 400 votes or fewer were cast

who_may_request: the candidate whose nomination is in question, in writing, received by the filing officer by 5:00 p.m. on the second day after the canvass of the primary

sources.quote: (2) a statewide federal office, state constitutional office, statewide judicial office, congressional office, or district judicial office is less than one-quarter of one percent of the total number of votes counted for that nomination or is ten votes or less and the total number of votes cast for the nomination is 400 votes or less

threshold.conditions: the requesting candidate files a request during the time for filing notice of contest of the primary or election, with a bond, cash or surety in an amount set by the filing officer; applies where the vote difference is greater than the difference that triggers the publicly funded recount
threshold.in_words: a losing candidate may have a manual recount at the candidate's own expense whatever the margin

who_may_request: a losing candidate whose name was on the ballot for a statewide federal, state constitutional, statewide judicial, congressional, state legislative or district judicial office
recounts.cost_bearer: the requesting candidate (bond, cash or surety); the jurisdiction pays instead if the optional recount changes the winner, or if the manual count differs from the election-night count by more than two votes and more than one-quarter of one percent of the ballots counted

sources.quote: A losing candidate whose name was on the ballot for nomination or election to a statewide federal office, state constitutional office, statewide judicial office, congressional office, state legislative office, or district judicial office may request a recount in a manner provided in this section at the candidate's own expense when the vote difference is greater than the difference required by this section.
If the winner of the race is changed by the optional recount, the cost of the recount must be paid by the jurisdiction conducting the recount.

recounts.note: Minn. Stat. 204C.35 subd. 2 (paragraphs (a), (b), (f) and (g)). The requester may name up to three precincts to be recounted first and waive the balance (paragraph (d)).

threshold.percent_of: the number of all other ballots cast at the election
threshold.in_words: when the 'yes' votes on ratification of a proposed constitutional amendment are within one-quarter percent of all the other ballots cast at the election, the canvassing board recounts that question by hand with no request

sources.quote: In a state general election when the difference between the number of "yes" votes cast on ratification of a proposed constitutional amendment is within one-quarter percent of the number of all other ballots cast at the election, the canvassing board shall manually recount the votes on that question

recounts.note: Minn. Stat. 204C.35 subd. 2a. The word "within" is read as including the boundary [inferred]; the denominator is all other ballots cast at the election, not the votes on the question.

threshold.in_words: the statute provides publicly funded and discretionary recounts for presidential electors under the same section, with a shortened deadline; the margin that makes one publicly funded is not separately stated for electors

who_may_request: a candidate, by 5:00 p.m. on the day after the canvass is completed
recounts.cost_bearer: publicly funded or discretionary as for the other races (see 204C.35)

sources.quote: Any request for recount for the election of presidential electors, whether publicly funded or discretionary, must be made by 5:00 p.m. on the day after the canvass is completed.

recounts.note: Minn. Stat. 204C.35 subd. 2b. That the statewide federal margin of one-quarter of one percent governs electors is a reading; the subdivision states only the timing (and that the recount is completed and certified within six days after it is requested).

threshold.percent_of: the total votes counted for that office
threshold.conditions: county, municipal or school district office; in an office with two or more seats the difference is between the elected candidate with the fewest votes and the non-elected candidate with the most
threshold.in_words: a losing candidate for a county, municipal or school district office may request a recount if the difference from a winning candidate is less than one-quarter of one percent of the votes counted

who_may_request: a losing candidate, in writing, to the county auditor (county offices) or the municipal or school district clerk, between the close of the canvass and 5:00 p.m. on the fifth day after a primary canvass or the seventh day after a special or general election canvass
recounts.cost_bearer: the county, municipality or school district

sources.quote: a losing candidate for nomination or election to a county, municipal, or school district office may request a recount of the votes cast for the nomination or election to that office if the difference between the vote cast for that candidate and for a winning candidate for nomination or election is less than one-quarter of one percent of the total votes counted for that office.

the county auditor shall recount the votes for a county office at the expense of the county, the governing body of the municipality shall recount the votes for a municipal office at the expense of the municipality, and the school board of the school district shall recount the votes for a school district office at the expense of the school district.

recounts.note: Minn. Stat. 204C.36 subd. 1(a) and (e). State general law only; a city charter may add to it and was not read.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes counted for that office
threshold.conditions: only where the total number of votes cast for the nomination or election of all candidates is more than 400 but less than 50,000
threshold.in_words: a losing candidate for a county, municipal or school district office may request a recount if the difference is less than one-half of one percent, where the total votes cast is more than 400 and less than 50,000

who_may_request: a losing candidate, as in the rule above
recounts.cost_bearer: the county, municipality or school district

sources.quote: is less than one-half of one percent, and the total number of votes cast for the nomination or election of all candidates is more than 400 but less than 50,000.

threshold.conditions: only where the total number of votes cast for the nomination or election of all candidates is no more than 400
threshold.in_words: a losing candidate for a county, municipal or school district office may request a recount if the difference is ten votes or less, where no more than 400 votes were cast

who_may_request: a losing candidate, as in the rule above
recounts.cost_bearer: the county, municipality or school district

sources.quote: is ten votes or less, and the total number of votes cast for the nomination or election of all candidates is no more than 400.

threshold.conditions: applies where the vote difference is greater than the difference required for the publicly funded recount; a bond, cash or surety set by the governing body of the jurisdiction must be filed
threshold.in_words: a losing candidate for a county, municipal or school district office may have a manual recount at the candidate's own expense whatever the margin

who_may_request: a losing candidate for nomination or election to a county, municipal or school district office
recounts.cost_bearer: the requesting candidate; the jurisdiction pays if the optional recount changes the winner or if the manual count differs from the election-night count by more than two votes and more than one-quarter of one percent of the ballots recounted

sources.quote: A losing candidate for nomination or election to a county, municipal, or school district office may request a recount in the manner provided in this section at the candidate's own expense when the vote difference is greater than the difference required by subdivision 1, paragraphs (a) to (e).

recounts.election: county, municipal or school district election

threshold.conditions: a written request with a petition of the signatures of 25 voters eligible to vote on the question; no bond when the difference between the votes for the question and the number required for passage is within the publicly funded difference of subdivision 1, a bond, cash or surety otherwise
threshold.in_words: any person eligible to vote on a local ballot question may request a recount with 25 voters' signatures; it is at the jurisdiction's expense within the subdivision 1 differences and at the requester's expense beyond them

who_may_request: any person eligible to vote on the ballot question, with a petition of 25 eligible voters
recounts.cost_bearer: the county, municipality or school district within the subdivision 1 difference; otherwise the person requesting, who files a bond, cash or surety

sources.quote: A recount for a ballot question may be requested by any person eligible to vote on the ballot question.

If the difference between the votes for the question and the number required for passage is greater than the difference provided in subdivision 1, the person requesting the recount shall also file with the filing officer of the county, municipality, or school district a bond, cash, or surety in an amount set by the appropriate governing body for the payment of recount expenses.

recounts.note: Minn. Stat. 204C.36 subd. 3. A statewide ballot question other than a constitutional amendment has no recount provision in 204C.35 as read.

unread.what: city and school district charters; Minn. Stat. chapter 209 (election contests); the text of any provision on a recount for a statewide question that is not a constitutional amendment

notes: This file extends the worked example: the first two recount rules and the first tie rule are the example's, re-checked against the page; the rest were read in this pass at the Revisor of Statutes' pages (204C.34 to 204C.36, chapter 208 and the Constitution).

Minnesota's recounts are all on a written request (there is no automatic recount of a candidate race); the publicly funded ones are free to the candidate within the thresholds, and a constitutional amendment within one-quarter percent is recounted without a request.
